subject: Animation
title: The Little Mermaid's Revival
description: A quick, practical guide to The Little Mermaid's Revival.

hook.text: In 1989, Disney released The Little Mermaid and ended two decades of animated mediocrity overnight.

buildup.text: Lyricist Howard Ashman brought Broadway-style musical storytelling to Disney for the first time.

discovery.text: Audiences fell in love with Ariel. The film earned $233 million and critical adoration worldwide.

twist.text: Disney executives had expected modest returns. Nobody predicted the film would start a revolution.

climax.text: The Little Mermaid launched a ten-year run of animated blockbusters that redefined the studio.

punchline.text: A singing mermaid resurrected Disney animation.

quiz.question: What made The Little Mermaid a turning point for Disney?
options: It was Disney's first animated film
It introduced Broadway-style musical storytelling and launched a decade of blockbusters
It was the first Disney film to use CGI

details.summary: The Little Mermaid in 1989 launched the Disney Renaissance, returning the studio to fairy tale musicals with Broadway-quality songs and vibrant animation. Its massive success proved that Disney's classic formula was not outdated — it just needed fresh creative energy.
details.whyItMatters: The Little Mermaid saved Disney animation and launched one of entertainment's most profitable creative eras. It proved that classic storytelling approaches succeed when executed with genuine passion and creative innovation.
takeaways: The Little Mermaid launched the Disney Renaissance in 1989
Howard Ashman and Alan Menken's Broadway-style music transformed Disney musicals
Its commercial and critical success proved Disney's animation formula remained viable

faq.question: What made The Little Mermaid different from previous Disney films?
faq.answer: Howard Ashman brought a Broadway musical sensibility to the storytelling. Songs advanced the plot and revealed character rather than just being pleasant interludes. Ariel was a more active, rebellious heroine than Disney's earlier princesses.

faq.question: How did The Little Mermaid change the animation industry?
faq.answer: Its box office success convinced studios that animated features could be blockbusters again. It launched a decade of animation investment across the industry, directly leading to competition from DreamWorks, Fox, and others trying to replicate Disney's formula.
